name: Power drill
description: A mains drill driver with a bit in the chuck. It only runs plugged in.
notes: Id shortened from the reference's. Drilling 2 sits above the hand drill's 1; screwing follows the reference. Needs mains or vehicle power, left to integration. CHECK VOLUME: the pistol shape and the cord coiled under the grip fill about six times the reference volume in their box.

name: Cordless drill
description: A battery drill driver with a bit in the chuck.
notes: Same frame as the power drill, standing on a slide-on battery pack. The impact wrench variant rides on this model: it would bring wrenching instead of drilling, set at integration. Battery use is left to integration. CHECK VOLUME: the pistol shape's box is about four times the reference volume.

name: Distaff and spindle
description: A long stick that holds combed fibre and a weighted spindle that twists it into yarn.
notes: Drawn as the distaff with a hank of fibre tied on, lying beside a drop spindle with a cop of yarn. Spinning is a new quality name. CHECK VOLUME: two thin rods lying apart give a box about five times the reference volume.

name: Electric breaker
description: A heavy battery demolition hammer with a T handle and a steel point. It breaks rock and concrete.
notes: Drawn lying down with its battery pack on the motor. Rock drilling 2 marks it above hand tools; how it breaks terrain and its power draw are left to integration. Two-handed. CHECK VOLUME: the T handle's span puts the box at about eight times the reference volume.

name: Fanning mill
description: A wooden grain cleaner. Turning the crank blows chaff away while the grain runs down the chute.
notes: A placed machine, so it carries a workstation rather than a tool quality, as the drill press does. Drawn as a tabletop mill on a stand with grain in the hopper; its box is 2.3 times the reference volume because the legs and drum leave open space.

name: Cut-off wheel
description: A thin abrasive wheel for an angle grinder. It cuts steel.
notes: One 230 mm wheel, which the reference weight fits. A spare part for an angle grinder; how a grinder takes it is left to integration.

name: Grinding wheel
description: A thick abrasive wheel with a dished centre, for an angle grinder. It grinds and shapes steel.
notes: One 180 mm depressed-centre wheel, thicker and smaller than the cut-off wheel so the two read apart.

name: Hacksaw
description: A fine-toothed blade held tight in a steel frame. It cuts metal, and wood slowly.
notes: metal_cutting 1, the hand grade below powered cutters, and sawing 1. CHECK LENGTH: a 12 inch blade with its frame and pistol grip is 41 cm, longer than the reference's 30 cm, which only fits the blade.

name: Bronze hammer
description: A rough-cast bronze head on a wooden haft. It drives nails well enough.
notes: Made by hand, so it is rare in the world. Hammering 1, below the steel hammer's 2. Its own row because the cast double-faced head differs from the hammer family's claw hammer. The melee block is left to integration, copying the hammer's.

name: Hand drill
description: A crank drill: turning the wheel spins the bit. Slow and tiring, but it needs no power.
notes: Drawn as an eggbeater drill. The makeshift hand drill rides on this model. CHECK VOLUME: the crown wheel and crank stand out from a thin frame, so the box is about six times the reference volume.

name: Rubber hose
description: A coil of flexible rubber hose. It can siphon fuel out of a tank.
notes: Siphoning is a new quality name. CHECK VOLUME: a coil is mostly air, so its box is about ten times the reference volume.

name: Garden hose
description: A coil of green garden hose. It can siphon fuel out of a tank.
notes: A variant of the rubber hose recoloured on the shared model. The real garden hose is three times the mass and longer; its own mass of 1.632 kg should be set at integration.

name: Makeshift jack
description: A small scissor jack bent up from scrap. It lifts a car if it holds.
notes: Made by the player, so usage is empty. Uses the scissor jack family with a rusted frame. Jacking 1 matches the scissor jack; the reference rates it higher, but a scrap jack should not outlift a factory one.

name: Petrol breaker
description: A petrol demolition hammer with a T handle and a steel point. It breaks rock and concrete, loudly.
notes: Drawn lying down with a two-stroke engine, fuel tank and pull starter at the handle end. Rock drilling 2 as the electric breaker; fuel use and terrain breaking are left to integration. Two-handed. CHECK VOLUME: the T handle and engine block put the box at about thirteen times the reference volume.

name: Electric kiln
description: A small top-loading kiln lined with fire brick. It fires clay and bricks on mains power.
notes: A placed machine, so it carries a workstation. firing is the quality name for firing clay, apart from charring. Needs mains or vehicle power, left to integration. CHECK VOLUME: drawn as a 30 cm hobby kiln, about four times the reference volume, because a smaller one cannot fire a brick.

name: Gunsmith repair kit
description: An aluminium case of gunsmithing tools: hammer, screwdrivers, files, a wrench, a punch, a small saw and a battery rotary tool.
notes: Drawn open with its lid standing so the tools show, as repair trays do. repairing 2 is its main job, above a general repair kit's 1; the others follow the reference at this game's scale, with kit grades at 1. Battery use per repair is left to integration. CHECK VOLUME: the open lid puts the box at about thirteen times the reference volume.
